note: Materialization corpus for the `duration` format. Every `wire` is VALID per the pinned duration regex (see format_duration/corpus.json). Rows are grouped by which design option they exercise. `full` = the whole accepted grammar (incl. Y/M/W); the design (B) custom struct must round-trip ALL of these byte-identically. `timeonly` = the narrowed PTnHnMnS-only subset that design (C) would materialize into a native fixed-duration type (Go time.Duration / Python timedelta / Java Duration); a materializing language must re-emit the CANONICAL string for these byte-identically. The CANONICAL form for the custom struct (B) is: reproduce the components verbatim in ISO order (PnYnMnDTnHnMnS, or PnW for the week form), omitting zero-valued components UNLESS the whole duration is zero, in which case emit PT0S. For (C) the canonical of a native fixed-duration is the same PTnHnMnS form derived from the total, so `PT1H` stays `PT1H`, `PT90M` normalizes-away-from-input (see NOTES: this is why native types cannot round-trip byte-identically for non-canonical time inputs).

timeonly_noncanonical.note: 90 min = 1h30m; a native total-based type CANNOT re-emit PT90M
Go keeps 24h; Java Duration.toString emits PT24H too - but see day boundary
